summary: Weekly POC security sync focusing on SSO/SAML testing, audit log exports, data retention options, SOC 2 artifacts, and next steps for validation during the pilot.
transcript: 00:00 Jordan Lee: okay uh good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. this is Jordan from Redwood, AE on the account. we have Priya the SE with me. 00:07 Priya Patel: hey team, hi, yeah excited to dig into the security items today. 00:12 Sam Torres: thanks, Jordan. quick note, we have Sam, Aisha and Liam on call. we put this on the calendar to validate the controls while we run the pilot. 00:20 Jordan Lee: perfect, agenda — quick review of last week's asks, SSO test status, audit-log/export format, retention settings, SOC2 docs and then next steps. sound good? 00:30 Aisha Khan: yep, go ahead. 00:33 Priya Patel: quick update on SSO: we created the SAML SP metadata and I uploaded it to your IdP test tenant, we also enabled SCIM provisioning but haven't run a full sync. there were a couple of attributes mapping questions, Sam, about mail vs userPrincipalName. 00:50 Sam Torres: yeah our IdP uses email as the primary. can you map to that? last time the mapping ended up on username field and we had duplicates. 00:58 Priya Patel: noted — we'll change mapping to email. also we did a smoke test of SSO login yesterday, one small hiccup where the ACS URL had an extra slash so the redirect failed, that was on our side and i pushed a fix. 01:14 Liam O'Neal: great. on the audit logs piece, we want to be sure we can get a full, tamper-evident export to feed into our SIEM. what's the retention and export cadence? 01:24 Jordan Lee: good q. by default hosted logs are retained 30 days, with streaming to customer SIEM as an add-on. we can provide daily or near-real-time streaming via S3 push or syslog connector. 01:36 Sam Torres: we need 13 months of immutable audit history for a subset of events for compliance, and we want to ensure integrity — are logs signed or otherwise verifiable? 01:46 Priya Patel: currently logs are delivered with a sequence id and tamper-evidence via write-once storage on our side; for enterprise customers we offer a signed manifest and hash chain upon request. we can also push to your S3 with server-side encryption and lifecycle rules you control. 02:02 Sam Torres: okay — will need written details. can you show an example schema? 02:06 Priya Patel: yes i'll share a sample export (JSON lines) that includes timestamp, actor, action, resource, request_id, session_id, and auth_context. expect that in the follow-ups. 02:17 Aisha Khan: about data retention — we have internal legal wants for deletion after 90 days for transient data but keeper logs for longer. what's Redwood's default and do you support field-level retention? 02:28 Jordan Lee: default's 30 days for workspace logs and 90 days for audit by contract; we have configurable retention windows per tenant, and we also support selective redaction/field-level retention for PII fields as part of the compliance package. 02:42 Sam Torres: is there an automated delete API so we can trigger deletes as part of a ticket flow? 02:48 Priya Patel: yes, we expose admin APIs to purge chat transcripts and artifacts and an audit API for deletion events; for hosted deployments some deletion is async and we emit a deletion-complete event that you can subscribe to. 03:00 Liam O'Neal: on SOC2, we need the Type II report and the supporting control narratives and that evidence mapping. can you provide the report and the list of controls mapped to product features? 03:12 Jordan Lee: absolutely, we'll send our latest SOC 2 Type II and the control mapping doc. full evidence isn't typically shared but we can provide control narratives and sample evidence artifacts redacted. 03:25 Sam Torres: any timelines? the procurement team asked for docs by EOD Friday. 03:29 Jordan Lee: we'll aim for Friday; Jordan: action to send SOC2 (Jordan). 03:33 Priya Patel: about encryption – at rest we use AES-256 and in transit TLS1.3. for BYOK we support KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and also HSM-backed keys for private instances. 03:46 Sam Torres: we are exploring BYOK; important that we maintain key ownership and key rotation. can Redwood rotate keys without seeing plaintext? 03:53 Priya Patel: yes, with BYOK the keys are customer-controlled; Redwood never has persistent access to your plaintext keys. rotations are coordinated and you can revoke keys which will force re-encryption flows depending on deployment. 04:07 Aisha Khan: regarding private network and VPC peering, we want to eyeball flow logs and the network ACLs. you support VPC peering for dedicated/private, right? 04:16 Jordan Lee: correct — dedicated and private deployments have VPC peering and controlled ingress via customer-managed subnets. for hosted we do egress whitelisting. 04:25 Sam Torres: okay good. also question about RBAC — we need role scoping for auditors so they can only read logs and not provision models. how granular is RBAC? 04:34 Priya Patel: RBAC is role- and permission-based; we have built-in roles (admin, dev, auditor) and allow custom roles with fine-grained permissions (read-only audit, deploy-only, billing-view). we can demo the auditor role in staging. 04:47 Liam O'Neal: can that tie into SCIM so that auditors are auto-provisioned with the right role? 04:52 Priya Patel: yes SCIM provisioning supports group-to-role mapping. 04:57 Jordan Lee: quick note on POC scope — the POC will exercise SSO login, SCIM provisioning for a small cohort, run a few generation workloads, capture associated audit logs, and validate retention/deletion flows. 05:10 Sam Torres: for the generation workloads we want to test PII redaction — if a user asks a model and sensitive info is returned, what's the data lifecycle? 05:20 Priya Patel: during the pilot we default to not use data for training; we have options for ephemeral KV cache and configurable persistence. any stored data is subject to tenant retention rules and can be redacted or purged via admin API. 05:35 Sam Torres: ok great. 05:38 Jordan Lee: a few clarifying items from legal: they asked about e-discovery and subpoena handling — do you have a standard process? 05:45 Priya Patel: we have a standard legal request process, we maintain a chain-of-custody for exports, and we can provide logs and exports to legal teams under subpoena; privacy team handles requests and we coordinate disclosures. 05:56 Aisha Khan: about the audit export format, can we get a sample of a daily batch and a streaming event shape? 06:02 Priya Patel: yes sample daily ND-JSON and a streaming event payload will be shared. 06:09 Jordan Lee: ok i'll summarize next steps near the end; for now any blockers on SAML testing? 06:15 Sam Torres: we tried the test metadata but got an attribute mismatch — that's our end to confirm with IdP. 06:20 Jordan Lee: okay we'll reopen mapping with you after the call. 06:24 Liam O'Neal: curious on performance impact of audit-level tracing — if we enable verbose audit for every token request, does latency increase? 06:33 Priya Patel: there's minimal overhead; the runtime writes lightweight traces and pushes async. heavy instrumentation can affect throughput marginally; we can toggle trace levels in staging to measure. 06:45 Sam Torres: for the logs to our SIEM we want signed manifests — is that available as part of the POC? 06:52 Priya Patel: yes we can enable signed manifests and provide an integrity hash chain for the export set, we'll include that in the sample. 07:01 Jordan Lee: procurement asked about indemnity and data residency clauses — any questions we should pre-empt? 07:07 Sam Torres: we need confirmation we can keep data in eu-west for our eu customers, and also a clause about ephemeral data not being used for training. 07:16 Jordan Lee: we support region pinning for hosted and dedicated, and a contract addendum for no-training telemetry by default. 07:23 Aisha Khan: can we get a short doc that spells out region options and the no-training language? 07:29 Jordan Lee: yes i'll include that with the SOC2 packet. 07:33 Priya Patel: a technical question from our side — Sam, will you want syslog or S3 delivery for logs? 07:39 Sam Torres: prefer S3 push initially, then maybe enable streaming to our SIEM. 07:45 Priya Patel: S3 push with server-side encryption + signed manifest, noted. 07:50 Jordan Lee: timeline check — SOC2 doc by Friday, SAML test user by next Tue, audit sample by Monday, RBAC demo next Wednesday? 07:58 Sam Torres: that timeline works. 08:02 Liam O'Neal: progress on the model quantization conversation — not security but affects private deployment options. 08:08 Priya Patel: brief — for private/dedicated we support mixed-precision quant and can provide runtime profiles; not a blocker for the security review. 08:16 Jordan Lee: ok to move into recap and actions. 08:20 Jordan Lee: recap: Jordan to send SOC2 Type II + region/no-training addendum; Priya to share audit-log sample, streaming formats, and enable signed manifest for POC; Jordan to create SAML test user and share metadata; Priya to run RBAC demo in staging and capture logs; Sam to confirm retention windows. any additions? 08:39 Sam Torres: could we also get a one-page summary of controls mapping to our security questionnaire? 08:44 Jordan Lee: yes, we'll include a controls mapping Q&A for the questionnaire. 08:49 Aisha Khan: thanks all. 08:51 Priya Patel: i'll follow up with the sample exports and the RBAC demo invite. 08:55 Jordan Lee: cool, thanks everyone — we'll follow up inline in the CRM and Slack. bye. 09:00 [meeting ends]
